newsitem.title: CONGO: New elephant watchdog born in Congo.
newsitem.headline: New elephant watchdog born in Congo.

text.p: A group hoping to protect elephants from ivory hunters launched itself in Congo on Saturday, one month after poachers killed 200 elephants in northwest Congo and took their tusks.

"The efforts of African states, bilateral and multilateral partners are already considerable in the region but they need to be supplemented by non-governmental organisations on the ground," founder Antoine Mapangui told journalists.

The new watchdog group, which includes researchers, academics, environmentalists and journalists, pledged to set up a surveillance network. It plans to use posters and radio and television to win over local people to the cause.
Mapangui said poaching in Central Africa had become "intense". Congo has about 8,000 elephants.
Trade in ivory is banned worldwide. The tusks of the 200 elephants killed in Sangha region in August were worth an estimated 150 million CFA francs ($291,000). Hippos are also at risk from poaching.
